name: MC33078DR2G
title: MC33078 / MC33079: low-noise dual and quad bipolar op amps
summary: A bipolar op amp family, two amplifiers per package (MC33078, NCV33078) or four (MC33079, NCV33079), aimed at audio and data signal paths. PNP input transistors give 4.5 nV/√Hz noise with 16 MHz gain bandwidth and 7 V/µs slew rate; the output stage is all NPN, without crossover deadband, and swings to +14.1 V / -14.6 V on ±15 V. It runs from ±5 V to ±18 V. The NCV parts are the automotive-qualified versions.

circuits.title: Figure 35. Voltage noise test circuit (0.1 Hz to 10 Hz p-p)
circuits.description: Two stages ahead of an oscilloscope, with an overall voltage gain of 50,000, for the 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz noise measurement. The device under test has its non-inverting input grounded and its inverting input tied to ground through 10 Ω, with 100 kΩ in parallel with 0.1 µF as feedback. A 2.0 kΩ and 4.7 µF low-pass feeds one half of an MC33078 wired non-inverting, 100 kΩ with 0.1 µF from output to inverting input and 24.3 kΩ to ground. Its output passes 4.3 kΩ into 2.2 µF to ground, then 22 µF in series to the scope input, which is loaded by 110 kΩ to ground; the scope is set to ×1 with 1.0 MΩ input.
notes: Every capacitor is non-polarised.

operation.text: Each amplifier has a PNP input pair chosen for low voltage noise at high bandwidth, and an output stage built only from NPN transistors that has no crossover deadband. Phase and gain margins are wide, open loop output impedance at high frequency is low, and sourcing and sinking behave alike at AC. The inputs carry ESD diodes.

Each input must stay within the supplies, never larger in magnitude than VCC or VEE; this sets both the input voltage and the input differential voltage ratings. Over -55 °C to 125 °C the common-mode range reaches from about 0.85 V to 0.45 V below VCC and from about 1.0 V to 0.75 V above VEE, the margin shrinking as temperature rises (Figure 7).

An output may be shorted indefinitely, provided the junction stays at or below 150 °C. Figure 2 gives the allowed dissipation against ambient temperature for each package: the DIPs allow the most, the SOIC-14 next and the SOIC-8 least, all falling to zero near 150 °C.

Gain and phase margin both fall as load capacitance rises (Figure 26), and step overshoot of a voltage follower rises with it, at 25 °C from about 11 % at 10 pF to about 39 % at 300 pF (Figure 27). With RL = 2.0 kΩ, typical phase margin is 55° with no load capacitance and 40° with 100 pF.

At a gain of +100, gain margin stays near 10.8 dB up to about 1 kΩ of differential source resistance and phase margin near 50° up to about 200 Ω; beyond those both fall steeply, phase margin reaching about zero near 16 kΩ and gain margin about 2 dB near 18 kΩ (Figure 30).
The NCV-prefixed parts carry automotive qualification, with site and change control to match.
